title: Telemetry-driven SLA Calibration and Handoff for Enterprise Onboarding
author: Priya Shah
body:
Summary

This playbook documents a telemetry-first approach to calibrating Service Level Agreements (SLAs) during enterprise customer onboarding, and the formal handoff from Customer Success (CS) to Production Operations / SRE. It is intended for CS leads, integration engineers, and production operations owners responsible for ensuring predictable inference economics and availability for new enterprise tenants.

Scope

- Applies to Hosted API and Dedicated (reserved-capacity) onboarding flows.
- Focuses on availability, tail latency, error rate, and cost signal alignment during the first 90 days post-provisioning.
- Does not replace contractual SLA language — this is an operational calibration & handoff procedure that maps telemetry to escalation and runbook actions.

Goals

1. Produce tenant-specific SLA targets informed by observed workload in the onboarding runway.
2. Define a deterministic, auditable handoff checklist from CS to SRE/Platform.
3. Ensure alerting and dashboards are in place with ownership and documented mitigation steps.

When to use this playbook

- Customer goes through enterprise onboarding and reaches the cutover/workload validation stage (typically week 2–6).
- Customer requests contract-level SLA profiling or has bespoke latency/cost targets.
- Early-production anomalies (cost spikes, tail latency regressions) require structured root-cause and adjustment of targets.

Roles and responsibilities

- Customer Success (CS) Lead: coordinates telemetry collection, customer communication, and initial run validation.
- Integration Engineer: implements telemetry tags, sample logs, and assists with synthetic tests.
- SRE / Production Ops Owner: configures final alerts, owns post-handoff incident response.
- Solutions Architect: recommends batching/quantization/routing changes when needed.

Key telemetry signals and mappings

- request_p95_latency_ms: primary latency indicator mapped to "SLO latency".
- request_p99_latency_ms: tail latency; escalation threshold mapping to incident response.
- request_error_rate_5m: 5-minute rolling error rate; triggers severity-2 at >=1%.
- tokens_per_second_per_tenant: throughput / cost proxy; used for cost-forecasting alerts.
- cache_hit_ratio_prefix: KV cache effectiveness; low values (>20% drop) trigger cache-investigation playbook.
- infra_utilization_gpu_pct: system-level signal — sustained >85% indicates capacity saturation.

Example mapping table (text table)

Metric | Observed threshold (onboarding) | Operational mapping
------ | ------------------------------ | ---------------------
request_p95_latency_ms | <= 250 ms (interactive apps) | Meet latency target: OK to hand off
request_p99_latency_ms | <= 800 ms | If >800ms for 3 consecutive days -> SRE review
request_error_rate_5m | < 0.1% | 0.1%–1% -> CS triage; >1% -> Page SRE
tokens_per_second_per_tenant | baseline from week-1 synthetic | Forecast cost and reserve capacity
cache_hit_ratio_prefix | > 70% | If drops by >20 percentage points -> investigate cache warming
infra_utilization_gpu_pct | < 65% | >85% sustained -> consider dedicated capacity / autoscale

Telemetry collection and tagging checklist (integration engineer)

1. Ensure all tenant-bound inference requests include tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, and flow_tags in telemetry headers and logs. Example JSON envelope: 

```
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-fin-001",
  "route_id": "chat-infer-v1",
  "model": "redwood-open-7b-q4",
  "flow_tags": ["interactive","high-priority"]
}
```

2. Emit per-request timing spans: client_enqueue, server_queue, decode_start, decode_end.
3. Emit token counts (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens) per request for cost attribution.
4. Instrument synthetic canary tests (see Synthetic test matrix below).

Synthetic test matrix (recommended)

- Warmup sequence: run 50 short inference requests (seq_len 32) to populate KV cache.
- Mixed load test: 10-minute run with 70% short (seq_len 32) + 30% long (seq_len 1024) at target TPS.
- Tail test: specific long-context requests (seq_len 4096) to confirm tail latency SLOs.

SLA calibration procedure (step-by-step)

1. Week-1 baseline (CS + integration engineer)
   - Run warmup and mixed synthetic tests at projected production TPS.
   - Collect 7 days of production-adjacent telemetry while customer runs in shadow/validation mode.
   - Compute baseline metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5m error rate, tokens/day, cache_hit_ratio.

2. Draft SLA targets (CS + solutions architect)
   - Use baseline metrics to propose tenant SLA bands: allow SLOs to be anchored to observed p95/p99 plus safety margin. Example: SLA_p95 = observed_p95 * 1.25 but capped to contract upper bound.
   - Document expected tail behavior for long-context requests and map to separate long-tail SLO (e.g., p99_long_seq).

3. Customer review and sign-off (CS + customer stakeholders)
   - Present telemetry summary, forecasted unit cost, and proposed SLOs in a short QBR-style deck.
   - Obtain explicit sign-off on targets or agreed-upon phase plan (e.g., Stage 1: soft SLOs for 30 days, Stage 2: hardened SLOs).

4. Handoff prep (CS + SRE) — minimum 48 hours before formal handoff
   - Ensure alert rules are implemented and tested in staging (see Monitoring queries).
   - Create tenant-specific dashboards and add to the SRE dashboard group.
   - Confirm on-call rotation and escalation contacts: primary SRE, secondary, CS on-call.

5. Formal handoff (SRE accepts ownership)
   - SRE runs synthetic verification and confirms alerts.
   - SRE documents runbook updates and acknowledges ownership in the handoff checklist.
   - CS schedules a 30-day checkpoint post-handoff for QBR alignment.

Acceptance criteria for handoff

- Required: 14 days of telemetry matching baseline behavior (no regressions >15% in p95 or error rate).
- Required: Tenant dashboard and 3 alerts configured (latency, error_rate, infra_utilization).
- Required: SRE runbook added to central runbook repo and owner acknowledged.
- Optional: Cost guardrails and quota caps configured if customer requires budget protection.

Monitoring queries (examples)

Prometheus-style example (replace label names as needed):

- p95 latency (ms):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_ms_bucket{tenant_id="acme-fin-001"}[5m])) by (le))
```
- error rate (5m percent):
```
(sum(rate(request_errors_total{tenant_id="acme-fin-001"}[5m]))) / (sum(rate(requests_total{tenant_id="acme-fin-001"}[5m]))) * 100
```
- GPU utilization (avg 1m):
```
avg by (instance) (rate(gpu_utilization_percent_total[1m]))
```
- cache hit ratio (5m):
```
(sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{tenant_id="acme-fin-001"}[5m]))) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total{tenant_id="acme-fin-001"}[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total{tenant_id="acme-fin-001"}[5m]))) * 100
```

Alerting thresholds (starter recommendations)

- Severity-1 (page): request_error_rate_5m > 3% for 5 minutes OR request_p99_latency_ms > 2000ms for 2 minutes.
- Severity-2 (notify + Slack): request_error_rate_5m between 1% and 3% for 10 minutes OR request_p95_latency_ms exceeds SLA_target by 30% for 10 minutes.
- Cost anomaly: tokens_per_hour increases by >150% relative to 7-day rolling average -> create investigation ticket.

Runbook excerpts (actions)

- On page (S1):
  1) Acknowledge page and add immediate note in incident tracker.
 2) Check tenant-specific dashboard for recent deploys, model variant, and queue depth.
 3) If infra_utilization_gpu_pct > 90% -> execute short-term scaling (burst or add capacity) and inform CS.
 4) If error spikes correlate with a specific model_variant -> fall back to last known-good variant using routing policy.

- On notify (S2):
  1) Post summary in tenant Slack channel and CC CS lead.
 2) Increase sampling of traces for affected route.
 3) Schedule triage within standard SRE response window (4 business hours).

Customer communications templates

- Pre-handoff sign-off confirmation (email):

Subject: [Action Required] SLA Calibration Summary & Handoff for {{tenant_name}}

Hi {{customer_contact}},

We completed 14 days of telemetry collection and synthetic validation for your environment. Attached is a short report with observed p95/p99 latency, error rates, and a cost forecast. Proposed operational SLAs: p95 <= {{SLA_p95}} ms; p99 <= {{SLA_p99}} ms; error rate < {{SLA_error}}%.

Please reply with approval or suggested changes. Once approved, we will schedule a formal handoff to our production ops team and enable tenant alerts.

Best,
{{cs_lead}}

Maintenance and post-handoff governance

- 30-day checkpoint: CS + SRE review telemetry and customer satisfaction.
- Quarterly reviews: incorporate QBR metrics and proposal for model/quantization changes that improve economics.
- Regression policy: any regression in p95 or error rate >20% post-handoff triggers an immediate joint triage and potential short-term rollback.

Operational notes and caveats

- Tail-sensitive workloads: for workloads that include sporadic long-context requests, maintain separate long-tail SLOs and make that explicit in the contract appendix.
- Warm caches: onboarded tenants that rely on prefix caching should expect a warm-up period; factor into SLA negotiation.

Appendix: Example dashboard widgets to include

- Tenant Overview: p50/p95/p99 latency trends (24h/7d), request rate, error rate.
- Cost attribution: tokens_per_hour, tokens_by_model, estimated $/hour.
- Capacity: GPU utilization, avg queue depth, instance count.
- Diagnostic traces: sample trace links for recent errors or high-latency requests.

Appendix: Quick CLI snippets for integration engineers

- Query recent tenant logs (example):
```
rdw logs query --tenant acme-fin-001 --from "-6h" --filter "route:chat-infer-v1" --limit 500
```
- Trigger synthetic test:
```
rdw synth run --tenant acme-fin-001 --test mixed-load --duration 10m --concurrency 10
```

Document maintenance and ownership

- Owner: Priya Shah (Customer Success) — maintain telemetry templates and sign-off checklist.
- Secondary owner: Miguel Torres (SRE) — owns alert rules and dashboard templates.
- Review cadence: biannual or when onboarding process changes materially.

Notes and references

- See related runbooks: tenant-stability-predictive-signals-runbook-2026.json for predictive signal definitions.
- See eng-platform dashboards for dashboard JSON templates.

End of document
